mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month jointly indicate a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls > -0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 55% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls > -1% AND HOUST falls > -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months, regardless of the business cycle phase, signals a deep labor market slack that consistently precedes negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes across all regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 0.4% for five consecutive months signals a robust demand expansion that boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
